summary.text: An 83-year-old male with 15-year type 2 diabetes, 7-year DKD and chronic renal failure, hypertension, heart failure and prior cerebral infarction had insulin aspart 30 and linagliptin before admission. Injection needles were infrequently replaced. Fatigue/dry mouth a week before admission prompted local assessment and transfer. Admission BP 143/86, pulse 86 and temperature 36.6°C accompanied an alert/oriented state, regular rhythm, soft abdomen and multiple periumbilical subcutaneous nodules/fat hyperplasia. Initial and imaging assessments documented renal impairment and several comorbid scan/ECG findings; routine scan modality is unspecified.

Continuous insulin and subsequent IV/pump/insulin degludec-liraglutide attempts did not stabilize daytime hyperglycemia/nocturnal hypoglycemia (narrative minimum 3.6 at 04:00; LAGE 28.7/SDBG 8.44). Drug interactions were excluded and abdominal imaging did not show insulinoma. Named chemiluminescence assays demonstrated marked serum insulin elevation, high IAA and insulin/C-peptide dissociation, supporting EIAS.

Insulin was discontinued; the narrative reports no further hypoglycemia but persistent hyperglycemia, prompting SC liraglutide 1.2 mg daily, oral dorzagliatin 75 mg twice daily and oral voglibose 0.2 mg three times daily. Glucose stabilized at 4.9–20.2 and later 6.8–17.6 mmol/L while insulin/IAA fell. Published serial measurements remain separate, including After 10 days glucose 3.14 despite the narrative absence claim. Possible LADA was not excluded; long-term C-peptide/autoantibody monitoring was recommended. Hormone therapy was not initiated.

summary.text: An 86-year-old male with 20-year type 2 diabetes, 10-year DKD, chronic renal failure and long-term routine hemodialysis had premixed lispro 25R before switching four months pre-admission to glargine/aspart. Each injection needle was reused ten times. Prostatic hyperplasia and hypertension and current tamsulosin/finasteride/amlodipine were documented. Admission temperature 36.8°C, pulse 76 and BP 123/76 accompanied normal cardiopulmonary/abdominal examination. Renal dysfunction and albumin 27.2 g/L were measured; scans/ECG/echo showed renal atrophy, cirrhosis, calcifications, cardiomegaly, complete RBBB, source-termed left artrial enlargement and impaired LV diastolic function.

Daytime glucose peaked at 29.0 and nocturnal glucose fell to 2.7 mmol/L between 02:00–06:00 (LAGE 26.9/SDBG 7.43). Renal failure/cirrhosis were initially considered causal. Increasing aspart, reducing glargine and adding linagliptin 5 mg daily did not eliminate fasting hypoglycemia/postprandial hyperglycemia. Antibody and insulin/C-peptide testing led to EIAS diagnosis; serial values include high IAA, GADA and marked insulin/C-peptide dissociation.

After stopping insulin, oral linagliptin 5 mg daily plus dorzagliatin 75 mg twice daily improved fluctuations but hypoglycemia persisted. Linagliptin was then stopped and oral acarbose 50 mg three times daily added, stabilizing glucose at 6–15 mmol/L. Follow-up serum insulin/IAA fell; possible concurrent LADA remained unexcluded and further C-peptide/autoantibody monitoring was recommended. Hormone therapy was not initiated. No discharge date is supplied.
